html:
The Addis Ababa to Djibouti railway is an electrified standard gauge line, opened in 2016, that links Addis Ababa, the capital of Ethiopia, with the port of Djibouti on the Gulf of Aden. It runs for about 750 km.

Ethiopia has had no coast since Eritrea became independent in 1993, and after the Eritrean Ethiopian War of 1998 to 2000 it lost the use of Eritrea's ports. Almost all its foreign trade now passes through Djibouti. An older narrow gauge line, the Ethio-Djibouti Railway, built by a French company and finished in 1917, had fallen into decay.

Chinese state companies built the new line, and Chinese banks lent most of the money, making it a flagship of what became the Belt and Road Initiative. A truck trip of several days became a train journey of under a day.

The railway has struggled with power cuts, debts and too little freight, and Ethiopia has had to renegotiate its loans. It remains the backbone of Ethiopia's plans for a national rail network.
